parts.problem_md:
A semicircle has a radius of 7 cm.

Find the area in terms of $π$.
parts.solution_md:
> *Draw a sketch of the semicircle, remember that the radius is from the centre to the edge of the circle*

![Diagram of a semicircle with a 14 cm diameter, split into two 7 cm sections. The radius is 7 cm, marked from centre to circumference.](assets/001-diagram-of-a-semicircle-with-a-14-cm-diameter-sp.png)

> *The formula for the area of a circle is *$πr^{2}$*, so the area of a semicircle will be half of this*

`1 half pi space r squared equals 1 half pi open parentheses 7 close parentheses squared`

**[M1]**

$\frac{1}{2}π\times49$

**Final answer:** $\frac{49}{2}π$** cm**<sup>**2**</sup>

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Method using half of the area of a circle.
> 
> **A1**: Correct final answer. May also be written as $\frac{49π}{2}$. Allow $24.5π$.

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

The diagram shows a circle, centre O, radius 11 cm. C, F, G and H are points on the circumference of the circle.

i) Find, in terms of $π$, the circumference of the circle.

[2]

ii)Work out angle $FOH$.

Angle $FOH$ = ................................................. [2]

iii) Calculate the length of the minor arc $FH$.

............................................ cm [2]
parts.solution_md:
(i) *Double the radius of the circle, 11 cm, to find the diameter, d.*

> * *$11\times2=22$* *

*Circumference =*** **$π\timesd$**.*** **Substitute in *$d=22$*, and leave your answer in terms of *$π$*. *

$22\timesπ=22π$

* ***[1]**

$22π$** [1]**

(ii) *Work out angle **OBC **by subtracting *$140^{\circ}$* from *$180^{\circ}$* (angles on a straight line add up to *$180^{\circ}$*).  *

`table row cell Angle space O B C end cell equals cell 180 minus 140 end cell row blank equals cell 40 degree end cell end table`

**[1]**

> *Angle **OBC** = angle **FOH **(**alternate **angles are equal). *

$40^{\circ}$* ***[1]**

(iii) *Write *$40^{\circ}$* (angle **FOH**) as a fraction of *$360^{\circ}$* (degrees in a full circle) and multiply by the circumference of the circle, *$22π$*.  *

$\frac{40}{360}\times22π=7.67944...$

**[1] **

*Round to 3 significant figures.*** **

**7.68 cm** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
![qp7d-0580-32-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/003-qp7d-0580-32-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

The diagram shows a square with vertices on the circumference of a circle, centre $O$. 
The radius of the circle is 6 cm.

Work out the shaded area.

.......................................... cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> *Work out the area of the circle by substituting *$r=6$* into *$A=πr^{2}$*.*

> * *$A=π\times6^{2}\,\,A=113.0973...$

* ***[1]**

> *Work out the area of one of the triangles by substituting **base = 6 **and **height = 6 **into **area = *$\frac{1}{2}$* x base x height**.*

> *(Because it is a square inside the circle, the dashed-line diagonals will meet at right angles at point **O**.)  *

$\frac{1}{2}\times6\times6=18$

* ***[1]**

> *There are 4 triangles in the middle of the circle, so multiply by 4. *

$18\times4=72$

* ***[1]**

> *Subtract the area of the triangles, 72 cm*<sup>*2*</sup>*, from the area of the circle, 113.0973... cm*<sup>*2*</sup>*, to find the shaded area. *

$113.0973...-72=41.0973...$

* ***[1]**

> *Round to 3 significant figures. *

**41.1 cm**<sup>**2**</sup> **[1]**

> *Substitute known values into the formula *$A=\frac{πr^{2}}{2}$* where *$r$* is the radius of the full circle*

$A=\frac{π\times8^{2}}{2}$

**[1]**

$=32π$

**[1]**

> *The area of a triangle is calculated using the formula *$A=\frac{b\timesh}{2}$* where *$b$* is the base and *$h$* is the perpendicular height.*

> *Substitute the known values into the formula and evaluate*

`A equals fraction numerator open parentheses 8 cross times 2 close parentheses cross times 8 over denominator 2 end fraction`

**[1]**

$=64$

**[1]**

> *Subtract the area of the triangle from the area of the semicircle to determine the area of the shaded region*

$32π-64$

$=36.53096491$

**36.5 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** (3sf)**** [1]**

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a rectangle and two semicircles with diameters $AC$ and $BD$. 
This diagram is a scale drawing of a running track. $AC=BD=60m\,AB=CD=120m$

![q9-058032-march2019-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/006-q9-058032-march2019-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

i) Complete the statement.

1 centimetre represents ............................ metres.

[2]

ii) Work out the total length of the running track in metres.

............................. m [3]

iii) Shreva walks at 1.4m/s.

Work out how long it will take her to walk once around the track. Give your answer in minutes and seconds, correct to the nearest second.

.................... minutes .................... seconds [3]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Using a ruler, measure the distance of *$CD$

$8\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *Divide the actual size by the measured length to determine the scale factor*

$120\div8=15m$

*1 centimetre represents **15 **metres***. [1]**

ii) *The circumference of a circle is calculated using the formula *$C=πd$*. *
*As the two parts of the running track between *$AC$* and *$BD$* are two identical semicircles, these create one full circle.*

> *Determine the circumference of this circle where *$d=60m$

$C=π\times60=188.4955592$

**[1]**

> *Add this distance to the two equivalent distances of *$CD$* and *$AB$

$120+120+188.4955592=428.4955592$

**[1]**

> *Round to 3 significant figures*

$428m$ **[1] **

**Or 428.4 or 428.5, or 428.49 to 428.52**

iii) *Substitute the values of *$D=428.5m$* and *$S=1.4m/s$* into the formula:*

> *Time = *$\frac{\mathrm{Distance}}{\mathrm{Speed}}$

$T=\frac{428.5}{1.4}=306.0714286$* seconds*

**[1]**

> *As *$300$* minutes is equivalent to *$5$* minutes*

$60\times5=300$* seconds*

**[1]**

> *the time in minutes and seconds is*

$5$** ****minutes **$6$** seconds** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
A circle has diameter 6 cm.

Calculate the area of the circle.

Give the units of your answer.
parts.solution_md:
> *Halve the diameter to find the radius. *

> $6\div2=3$* *

> *Substitute r = 3 into the formula for the area of a circle, area = *$\mathrm{πr}^{2}$

$\mathrm{area}=π\times3^{2}$ **[1]**

> *Type into a calculator. *

> $π\times3^{2}=28.2743...$* *

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

`28.2743... space equals space 28.3 space open parentheses 3 sf close parentheses`

> *The unit is *$\mathrm{cm}^{2}$* because we have found an **area**.*

$28.3\mathrm{cm}^{2}$* ***[2]**

**one mark is for correct units**

**28.27 - 28.28 accepted**
